I'm putting the report together now, and I want to be upfront that I couldn't observe the 12-minute process directly. My best guess is that it was the waiting step.

I opened PR #2406: https://github.com/openagt/openagent/pull/2406. With the fix, the dashboard no longer keeps a naming process around after the name is given.

**Why it stayed alive:** I couldn't see the process you saw, so this is the most likely cause rather than a certainty. Once the name is given, the session that answered is killed straight away. But the dashboard then starts a new naming session at once, for whatever run comes next, and lets it wait up to 20 minutes (`packages/agent-driver/core/src/engine/ready-naming.ts`). When it expires, another one replaces it, with no end. So the dashboard always had a `claude -p` running in an `openagent-naming-…` folder, even if nobody started another run. A 12-minute-old one is what that design produces. I also found this process's replacements still running on this machine.

**What changed:**
- **Dashboard:** the naming process is killed once it answers, and no new one is started after a name or after a timeout. The next one starts only when the launcher opens or its agent changes, which already happened before.
- **Shorter wait:** a session started for a run that never comes is killed after 5 minutes instead of 20. That number is my choice. Someone who types for longer than 5 minutes gets their name in about 2 seconds instead of 1.
- **Inside a run:** `nameRun` in `title.ts` now kills its own naming process after the answer. Before, it relied on `claude` exiting on its own and had nothing to kill it if it didn't.

**Tests:** I added four tests in which the fake agent stays alive after answering until it is killed. All four fail on the old code and pass with the fix. Typecheck passes, and so do the tests of `@openagt/agent-driver` and every package that depends on it. `pnpm`'s `'...[origin/main]'` filter matches no packages in this worktree, so I named the package directly instead.
